newsitem.title: SPAIN: Spain blames Cuba for envoy crisis but ties remain.
newsitem.headline: Spain blames Cuba for envoy crisis but ties remain.

text.p: Spain blamed Cuba on Tuesday for a crisis in bilateral relations but said it wanted to keep diplomatic ties in place.
"Cuba does not want to start (democratic) reforms...that's the problem," Spanish Foreign Minister Abel Matutes told a news conference. But he added: "We want to maintain relations with Cuba."
Relations between Cuba and Spain have been increasingly strained as a result of Madrid's new get-tough stance since a conservative government took office in May.
They came to the brink of breakdown earlier on Tuesday when Havana denounced what it called "flagrant interference" in its affairs.

To underscore its protest, Cuba's Communist government withdrew its previously given acceptance of a new Spanish ambassador -- a move diplomats in Madrid said was the toughest possible short of breaking relations.

Matutes's assurances that Spain wants ties with Cuba to remain in place sounded more mellow than his earlier first reaction to Havana rejection of the new ambassador, when he described the move as "a big mistake".
